Alex — great talking earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. TL;DR: you said target is roughly $1,000–$2,500 net acquisition cost per paying customer and you want core feature unit cost to be < $15 per active feature / month at scale. You also called out a target inference spend envelope of ~$1M tokens/month initially, moving toward 5–10M.

Call highlights:
- Product scope: in-app summarization + ranking + 2x contextual prompts per user session. Estimated token mix: 25% long (avg 2k tokens), 75% short (avg 150 tokens).
- Volume timing: pilot (Q4) ~1k DAUs, scale (Q2-Q3) to 10k DAUs.
- Commercial goal: confirm if Redwood can produce an estimate of $/feature (per month) and model-level $/1M tokens to evaluate unit economics + CAC payback at 6–9 months.

Proposed next steps (action owners & dates):
1) Sean (me): produce a baseline unit-econ sketch (token-level $/1M + per-feature amortized cost) — delivering by Thu 8/26 EOD.
2) Dev (SE): validate plausibility of quantization/batching assumptions and provide latency vs cost tradeoffs — deliver Thurs 8/26 EOD.
3) FinLytics (Alex/Karen): confirm expected monthly token volumes by feature (spreadsheet attached if helpful).
4) Monica: follow up on proposed commercial packaging and potential trial credits.

Attachments: I pushed a lightweight TCO template (finlytics_tco_model.xlsx) to the Drive link; drop your numbers there.

If any of the summary points here are off, flag and I’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll send the econ sketch tomorrow.

Alex — thanks for the quick upload. Based on your numbers and our performance profiles I sketched a conservative baseline. High-level economics (pilot scale -> steady state):

1) Token-level pricing estimate (Redwood hosted):
- Long-context calls (avg 2k tokens): ~14 calls/day per DAU during active sessions in pilot; cost = $0.45 per 1k tokens (model mix infra/quantized + batching assumptions) => ~$900 per 1M tokens effective for long-context mix (includes batching gains).
- Short calls (avg 150 tokens): cost-effective $/1k = $0.10 => ~$100 per 1M tokens.
- Blended early-stage estimate: ~$420 per 1M tokens given 25% long / 75% short mix.

2) Per-feature monthly amortized cost (assuming pilot: 1k DAUs, 20% active, 2 sessions/day):
- Summarization (40% of sessions): ~$2.8k/month total => per-active-feature per-month = ~$2.8 (spread across all DAUs).
- Ranking (20% of sessions): ~$1.1k/month total => per-active-feature per-month = ~$1.1.
- Combined feature stack incremental cost (summarization + ranking + prompts overhead): ~ $4.5k/month => per-DAU basis ~ $4.50/month or per-feature ~ $4.50 aggregated.

3) Projection to scale (10k DAUs): economies of scale from batching/prefix caching and model quantization uplift can push blended $/1M tokens to ~$280–$320 and per-feature $/month toward ~$0.40–$0.60 per DAU depending on retention.

4) CAC payback quick check: with a target LTV/CAC where CAC=$2,000 and ARR per customer (avg 3 paid features) at $180/year (est), payback looks marginal at pilot unless gross margins are improved by 10–15% via pricing or credits. We modeled payback at ~8–12 months post-scale with 30% net margins.

I attached a simple summary table (pasted below) and exported the TCO sheet to PDF for your finance team. If you want I can convert the blended model into scenarios (best / base / worst) by EOD.

Sean

Alex / Sean — quick technical validation and tradeoffs to sanity-check the econ sketch. Key assumptions and margin levers:

1) Quantization profile: 8-bit Q4 followed by per-kernel fusion gives ~2.6x cost reduction vs fp16 on A100-like infra. We can expect slightly lower throughput for very long-context calls but acceptable latency under your 1.2s p95 for summarization.

2) Batching behavior: pilot batching window set to 15–30ms will preserve short-flow latency (~<350ms p95) while still aggregating enough requests to meaningfully cut per-token runtime. At scale, continuous batching + KV caching for repeated contexts (session affinity) can reduce effective token compute by ~12–18% for your use case.

3) Model routing: recommend mixed routing — short flows to a trimmed 7B quantized model for ranking, long summarization to a heavier 13B quantized model with prefix caching. This keeps blended quality high while preserving cost targets.

4) Cost sensitivity table (approx):
- If token volumes + long-call mix increase by 30% without pricing changes => blended $/1M -> ~$540.
- If we improve caching + batching at scale -> blended $/1M -> ~$260.

I can produce a small matrix (CSV) of scenarios mapping token volume / long-call fraction / batching efficiency -> $/1M tokens. Will attach that CSV to the Drive folder in an hour.

Happy to review numbers on a call with your infra/finance folks.

Thanks,
